My father grew wheat and maize on this land. His father did too. The soil here on the Hebei Plain is good for it, and the buyers come reliably. I have 10 mu. I know what works.

**My thinking:**

For winter, I plant wheat — all 10 mu. That's what we do here. Planting starts in October after I plough with the hired tractor. I'll buy improved seed from the township seed shop, whatever the shop owner says is selling well this year — probably a Jimai or Zhengmai variety. For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer at sowing, then I top-dress with urea before jointing in spring. I try to put down enough — losing yield hurts more than spending a little extra on fertilizer. I water four times: before winter sets in, after green-up, at jointing, and at grain filling. I've lost a crop to aphids before, so I spray twice minimum.

Come June after harvest, I plant maize immediately on the same 10 mu. No time to waste — the season is short. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or similar, everyone around here uses it. I do rotary tillage before planting. Maize doesn't need as much water if summer rains come, but I irrigate once at establishment and again if August is dry. I spray herbicide right after planting and check for corn borer in July.
